main: Hard work is important if we want to achieve our goals. Many successful people did not succeed immediately. They worked hard for a long time before reaching their dreams. Hard work helps us learn new skills and gain experience. Sometimes, we may fail, but failure teaches us important lessons. Some people believe talent is the most important thing, but even talented people need to work hard. If we keep trying and never give up, we can improve and get closer to our dreams.
Q1A: A. The value of hard work.
Q1B: B. How to relax more.
Q1C: C. The best way to become rich.
A1: A. The value of hard work.
Q2: What can failure teach us?
Q2A: A. How to avoid hard work.
Q2B: B. Important lessons.
Q2C: C. How to relax.
A2: B. Important lessons.
japanese: 目標を達成するためには努力が重要です。多くの成功した人々はすぐには成功しませんでした。彼らは夢を達成する前に長い間努力してきました。努力は新しいスキルを学び，経験を積む手助けをします。時には失敗することもありますが，失敗は大切な教訓を教えてくれます。才能が最も重要だと信じる人もいますが，才能がある人でも努力は必要です。もし私たちが努力し続け，決して諦めなければ，改善し，夢に近づくことができるのです。

main: Friends make our lives happier and more meaningful. A good friend supports us when we are sad and celebrates with us when we are happy. Friendship also teaches us kindness and trust. Some friendships last for many years, while others are short, but all friendships are valuable. However, good friendships need effort. We should listen to our friends and help them when they need us. If we take care of our friendships, they can bring us joy for a lifetime.
Q1A: A. The importance of friendship.
Q1B: B. The history of school.
Q1C: C. The best way to become famous.
Q1D: D. Why studying alone is best.
A1: A. The importance of friendship.
Q2: What does the passage say about friendship?
Q2A: A. It is not important in life.
Q2B: B. Friendships never need effort.
Q2C: C. We should support and listen to our friends.
Q2D: D. Only childhood friendships are valuable.
A2: C. We should support and listen to our friends.
japanese: 友だちは私たちの人生をより幸せで意味のあるものにしてくれます。良い友だちは、私たちが悲しいときに支えてくれ，うれしいときには祝ってくれます。友情はまた思いやりや信頼を教えてくれます。長く続く友情もあれば，短い友情もありますが、すべての友情は大切です。しかし，良い友情には努力が必要です。私たちは友だちの話をよく聞き，助けが必要なときには手を差し伸べるべきです。友情を大切にすれば，それは一生の喜びをもたらしてくれるでしょう。

main: The environment is very important for all living things. However, pollution and climate change are big problems today. People throw away too much plastic, and many forests are cut down. These actions harm animals and nature. To protect the environment, we should recycle, save energy, and use less plastic. Even small actions like turning off lights and using reusable bags can help. If we all work together, we can make the world a cleaner and safer place for future generations.
Q1A: A. The importance of sports.
Q1B: B. Saving the environment.
Q1C: C. How to travel the world
A1: B. Saving the environment.
Q2: What does the passage suggest for helping the environment?
Q2A: A. Using more plastic.
Q2B: B. Cutting down more trees.
Q2C: C. Recycling and saving energy.
A2: C. Recycling and saving energy.
japanese: 環境はすべての生き物にとってとても重要です。しかし、今日では汚染や気候変動が大きな問題となっています。人々はプラスチックを捨てすぎ、たくさんの森林が伐採されています。これらの行動は動物や自然に害を与えます。環境を守るために、私たちはリサイクルを行い、エネルギーを節約し、プラスチックの使用を減らすべきです。電気を消すことや、再利用可能な袋を使うことのような小さな行動でも助けになります。もし私たち全員が協力すれば、将来の世代のために世界をより清潔で安全な場所にすることができます。

main: Music has the power to change our emotions. Happy songs can make us feel energetic, while slow and soft music helps us relax. Some people listen to music when they study because it improves their focus. Others use music to express their feelings. Playing an instrument or singing can be a great way to relieve stress. Music is also important in celebrations and ceremonies. No matter what kind of music we like, it makes our lives richer and more enjoyable.
Q1A: A. The best way to study.
Q1B: B. How music affects our feelings.
Q1C: C. The history of musical instruments.
Q1D: D. Why people should learn music.
A1: B. How music affects our feelings.
Q2: What does the passage say about music?
Q2A: A. It has no effect on emotions.
Q2B: B. It helps people relax and focus.
Q2C: C. Only playing an instrument is enjoyable.
Q2D: D. Music is not used in celebrations.
A2: B. It helps people relax and focus.
japanese: 音楽には私たちの感情を変える力があります。楽しい曲は私たちを元気にし、ゆっくりとした柔らかい音楽はリラックスさせてくれます。勉強するときに音楽を聴く人もいますが、それは集中力を高めてくれるからです。ほかの人は、自分の気持ちを表すために音楽を使います。楽器を演奏したり歌ったりすることは、ストレスを和らげる素晴らしい方法にもなります。音楽はお祝いの場や儀式においても大切です。私たちがどんな種類の音楽を好んでも、それは私たちの生活をより豊かで楽しいものにしてくれます。

main: Cooking is not just about making food; it is an important life skill. When people learn to cook, they can prepare healthy meals and save money instead of eating out. Cooking also helps develop creativity, as people try new ingredients and recipes. Some families cook together, making it a fun and educational activity. Additionally, knowing how to cook allows people to make food that suits their tastes and dietary needs. Cooking is a skill that benefits people throughout their lives.
Q1A: A. Cooking as a life skill.
Q1B: B. The history of cooking.
Q1C: C. Why eating out is bad.
Q1D: D. How to become a professional chef.
A1: A. Cooking as a life skill.
Q2: According to the passage, what is one benefit of cooking?
Q2A: A. It helps people save money.
Q2B: B. It is only for professional chefs.
Q2C: C. It is not useful in daily life.
Q2D: D. It makes food less enjoyable.
A2: A. It helps people save money.
japanese: 料理はただ食べ物を作ることではなく，重要な生活スキルです。料理を学ぶと，外食をする代わりに健康的な食事を作り，お金を節約することができます。また，料理は新しい食材やレシピに挑戦することで創造性を育てます。家族で一緒に料理をする家庭もあり，それは楽しく学びのある活動になります。さらに，料理の方法を知っていると，自分の好みや食事の制限に合った料理を作ることができます。料理は一生を通じて人々に役立つスキルなのです。

main: Walking is one of the easiest ways to stay healthy. It strengthens the heart, muscles, and bones. Walking outside also helps reduce stress and improve mood. Many people walk to school or work, which helps them stay active. Even short walks during the day can have positive effects on the body. Walking in nature is especially relaxing. Unlike other exercises, walking does not require special equipment. Anyone can do it, making it a simple yet effective way to stay fit.
Q1A: A. The benefits of walking.
Q1B: B. The dangers of exercise.
Q1C: C. Why running is better than walking.
A1: A. The benefits of walking.
Q2: What does the passage say about walking?
Q2A: A. It requires special equipment.
Q2B: B. It helps reduce stress and improve mood.
Q2C: C. People should only walk indoors.
Q2D: D. Walking is a difficult exercise.
A2: B. It helps reduce stress and improve mood.
japanese: 歩くことは、健康を保つための最も手軽な方法のひとつです。心臓、筋肉、骨を強くしてくれます。外を歩くことはストレスを減らし、気分を改善する効果もあります。多くの人が学校や職場まで歩いており、それが活動的でいることにつながっています。日中の短い散歩でも、体に良い影響があります。自然の中を歩くと、特にリラックスできます。他の運動と違い、歩くために特別な道具は必要ありません。誰でもできるため、シンプルでありながら効果的なフィットネス方法です。

main: The night sky is full of wonders. The moon changes shape every night, and stars shine brightly. Sometimes, people can see shooting stars or even planets with a telescope. For thousands of years, humans have studied the stars and created stories about them. Watching the night sky can be relaxing and make people feel curious about the universe. Whether in a city or the countryside, looking up at the stars reminds us of how big and beautiful the world is.
Q1A: A. Why stars are not important.
Q1B: B. The history of space travel.
Q1C: C. The beauty of the night sky.
Q1D: D. How to become an astronaut.
A1: C. The beauty of the night sky.
Q2: What does the passage say about watching the night sky?
Q2A: A. It can be relaxing and inspiring.
Q2B: B. It is only for scientists.
Q2C: C. People should not look at the stars.
Q2D: D. The night sky is not interesting.
A2: A. It can be relaxing and inspiring.
japanese: 夜空は不思議なもので満ちています。月は毎晩形を変え、星は明るく輝きます。時には流れ星を見たり、望遠鏡を使って惑星を見ることもできます。何千年もの間、人類は星を研究し、それについての物語を作ってきました。夜空を眺めることは心を落ち着かせ、宇宙への好奇心をかき立ててくれます。都市でも田舎でも、星を見上げることで、世界がどれほど大きく美しいかを思い出させてくれます。

main: Mistakes are a natural part of life, and they help us grow. When people fail, they have a chance to think about what went wrong, make changes, and try again. Many successful people, like inventors, athletes, and scientists, have failed many times before reaching their goals. Each mistake teaches them something new and helps them improve. Instead of feeling bad about mistakes, we should see them as learning opportunities. Making mistakes is not a sign of weakness; it is a step toward success and a way to become stronger.
Q1A: A. The importance of learning from mistakes
Q1B: B. Why people should avoid failure
Q1C: C. The history of success
A1: A. The importance of learning from mistakes
Q2: According to the passage, what should people do when they make mistakes?
Q2A: A. Feel bad about them
Q2B: B. Learn from them and improve
Q2C: C. Give up on their goals
A2: B. Learn from them and improve
japanese: 失敗は人生の自然な一部であり、私たちが成長するのを助けてくれます。人は失敗したとき、何が悪かったのかを考え、改善し、もう一度挑戦する機会を得ます。発明家、アスリート、科学者など、多くの成功した人々は、目標を達成する前に何度も失敗しています。それぞれの失敗は彼らに新しいことを教え、向上するのを助けてくれます。失敗について落ち込むのではなく、それを学ぶ機会として捉えるべきです。失敗することは弱さの表れではなく、成功への一歩であり、より強くなるための方法なのです。

main: Laughter is a simple but powerful tool for happiness. When we laugh, our body releases chemicals that reduce stress, help us stay healthy, and improve our mood. Scientists say that people who laugh often feel happier and may live longer. Laughing with friends makes relationships stronger, and watching funny movies or telling jokes is a great way to relax. Even when life is hard, a little laughter can make us feel better and help us keep going. A good sense of humor makes life more enjoyable and brings people closer together.
Q1A: A. The benefits of laughter.
Q1B: B. The history of comedy.
Q1C: C. Why people should be serious.
Q1D: D. How to become a comedian.
A1: A. The benefits of laughter.
Q2: What is one effect of laughter?
Q2A: A. It increases stress.
Q2B: B. It improves mood and health.
Q2C: C. It makes people live shorter lives.
Q2D: D. Only jokes can make people laugh.
A2: B. It improves mood and health.
japanese: 笑いは、シンプルですが幸福のための強力なツールです。私たちが笑うとき、体はストレスを減らし、健康を保ち、気分を向上させる化学物質を放出します。科学者たちは、よく笑う人はより幸せを感じ、長生きする可能性があると言っています。友達と一緒に笑うことは人間関係をより強固にし、面白い映画を見たり冗談を言ったりすることはリラックスするための素晴らしい方法です。人生が困難な時でさえ、少しの笑いが私たちの気分を良くし、前進し続けるのを助けてくれます。良いユーモアのセンスは人生をより楽しいものにし、人々をより身近な存在にしてくれます。

main: Eating vegetables is very important for our health. Vegetables have many vitamins that help our body stay strong. People who eat a lot of vegetables have more energy and do not get sick easily. However, some people do not like vegetables because of their taste. To eat more vegetables, we can try different ways of cooking them. For example, mixing vegetables with meat or making a soup can make them taste better. Eating vegetables every day is a good habit. It helps us stay healthy and feel good.
Q1A: A. The importance of vegetables.
Q1B: B. The best way to cook meat.
Q1C: C. How to avoid getting sick.
Q1D: D. The dangers of eating too much.
A1: A. The importance of vegetables.
Q2: What does the passage suggest about eating vegetables?
Q2A: A. It is bad for health.
Q2B: B. People should not eat them every day.
Q2C: C. Cooking them in different ways can help.
Q2D: D. Only children need to eat vegetables.
A2: C. Cooking them in different ways can help.
japanese: 野菜を食べることは私たちの健康にとって非常に重要です。野菜には、体を強く保つのに役立つビタミンがたくさん含まれています。野菜をたくさん食べる人はよりエネルギーがあり、簡単には病気になりません。しかし、その味が理由で野菜が好きではない人もいます。より多くの野菜を食べるために、さまざまな調理方法を試すことができます。例えば、野菜を肉と混ぜたりスープにしたりすることで、より美味しくすることができます。毎日野菜を食べることは良い習慣です。それは私たちが健康を保ち、気分良く過ごすのに役立ちます。

main: Being on time is an important habit that benefits both ourselves and others. It shows respect, responsibility, and good time management skills. People who are always late may miss important events, lose opportunities, or cause inconvenience to others. To be punctual, planning ahead, setting reminders, and preparing in advance can be helpful. Those who are on time often feel less stressed, stay more organized, and earn a better reputation. Whether at school, work, or social gatherings, being punctual helps build trust and leads to greater success in life.
Q1A: A. Why being on time matters.
Q1B: B. The history of clocks.
Q1C: C. How to sleep longer.
Q1D: D. Why people should be late.
A1: A. Why being on time matters.
Q2: According to the passage, why is being on time important?
Q2A: A. It helps build trust and success.
Q2B: B. It makes life more stressful.
Q2C: C. It is not necessary for school.
Q2D: D. Only adults need to be on time.
A2: A. It helps build trust and success.
japanese: 時間を守ることは、自分自身と他者の両方に利益をもたらす重要な習慣です。それは、敬意、責任感、そして優れた時間管理スキルを示します。いつも遅刻する人は、重要な出来事を逃したり、機会を失ったり、他人に迷惑をかけたりする可能性があります。時間を守るためには、事前に計画を立て、リマインダーを設定し、前もって準備することが役立ちます。時間を守る人は、ストレスをあまり感じず、より整理された状態を保ち、より良い評判を得ることがよくあります。学校でも、職場でも、社交の場でも、時間を守ることは信頼を築くのに役立ち、人生におけるより大きな成功につながります。

main: Reading books opens the door to new worlds. Through stories, we can visit faraway places and meet people from different times. Reading also helps us learn new words and think more deeply. Students who read often usually write better, too. Some people say they have no time to read, but even ten minutes a day can make a difference. Choosing a book you enjoy is the key. When reading becomes a habit, it stays with us for life and keeps our minds active.
Q1A: A. How to write a novel.
Q1B: B. The value of reading books.
Q1C: C. The history of libraries.
Q1D: D. Why stories are not true.
A1: B. The value of reading books.
Q2: What does the passage say about time for reading?
Q2A: A. People need at least two hours a day.
Q2B: B. Reading is only for weekends.
Q2C: C. Even ten minutes a day can help.
Q2D: D. Busy people should not read.
A2: C. Even ten minutes a day can help.
japanese: 本を読むことは、新しい世界への扉を開きます。物語を通して、私たちは遠く離れた場所を訪れたり、異なる時代の人々に出会ったりすることができます。また、読書は新しい言葉を学び、より深く考える助けにもなります。よく本を読む生徒は、たいてい文章を書くのも上手です。読書をする時間がないと言う人もいますが、1日10分でも違いを生むことができます。自分が楽しめる本を選ぶことが鍵です。読書が習慣になれば、それは一生続き、私たちの頭を活発に保ってくれます。

main: Getting enough sleep is just as important as eating well. While we sleep, our body repairs itself and our brain organizes what we learned during the day. Teenagers need about eight to ten hours of sleep each night. Without it, they may feel tired, lose focus in class, and become easily upset. Using a phone late at night can make it harder to fall asleep. Going to bed at the same time every day helps our body build a healthy rhythm.
Q1A: A. Why teenagers love phones.
Q1B: B. The best food for dinner.
Q1C: C. How dreams are made.
A1: D. The importance of sleep.
Q2: What can make it harder to fall asleep?
Q2A: A. Going to bed at the same time.
Q2B: B. Using a phone late at night.
Q2C: C. Eating well.
A2: B. Using a phone late at night.
japanese: 十分な睡眠をとることは、しっかり食べることと同じくらい重要です。眠っている間に、体は自らを修復し、脳はその日に学んだことを整理します。10代の若者には、毎晩およそ8～10時間の睡眠が必要です。睡眠が足りないと、疲れを感じたり、授業に集中できなくなったり、すぐにいらいらしたりすることがあります。夜遅くにスマートフォンを使うと、寝つきが悪くなることがあります。毎日同じ時間に寝ることで、体は健康的なリズムを作ることができます。

main: Smartphones have changed the way we live. With one small device, we can call friends, take pictures, check the news, and find information in seconds. They are very useful, especially when we travel or need help quickly. However, spending too much time on smartphones can cause problems. Some people stop talking to the people around them, and others have trouble sleeping. It is important to decide when to use our phones and when to put them away. Smartphones are helpful tools, but we should control them, not let them control us.
Q1A: A. The history of the telephone.
Q1B: B. How to take good pictures.
Q1C: C. Using smartphones wisely.
A1: C. Using smartphones wisely.
Q2: What problem can smartphones cause?
Q2A: A. They make information hard to find.
Q2B: B. People may stop talking to others around them.
Q2C: C. They make travel impossible.
A2: B. People may stop talking to others around them.
japanese: スマートフォンは私たちの生活の仕方を変えました。小さな機器ひとつで、友だちに電話をかけたり、写真を撮ったり、ニュースを確認したり、数秒で情報を見つけたりすることができます。特に旅行中やすぐに助けが必要なときには、とても役に立ちます。しかし、スマートフォンに時間を使いすぎると、問題が起こることがあります。周りの人と話をしなくなる人もいれば、眠れなくなる人もいます。いつスマートフォンを使い、いつしまうかを決めることが大切です。スマートフォンは便利な道具ですが、私たちがスマートフォンをコントロールすべきであり、スマートフォンに振り回されてはいけないのです。

main: Learning a foreign language can be difficult, but it is also exciting. When we learn a new language, we can talk with people from other countries and understand their cultures. It also gives us more chances to find good jobs in the future. Many learners feel shy about speaking because they are afraid of making mistakes. However, speaking is the fastest way to improve. Watching movies, listening to songs, and chatting online are fun ways to practice. Little by little, a new language can open many doors.
Q1A: A. The benefits of learning a foreign language.
Q1B: B. How to find a job.
Q1C: C. The history of movies.
A1: A. The benefits of learning a foreign language.
Q2: According to the passage, what is the fastest way to improve?
Q2A: A. Reading grammar books.
Q2B: B. Staying silent.
Q2C: C. Speaking.
A2: C. Speaking.
japanese: 外国語を学ぶことは難しいこともありますが、わくわくすることでもあります。新しい言語を学ぶと、他の国の人々と話し、その文化を理解することができます。また、将来良い仕事を見つけるチャンスも増えます。多くの学習者は、間違えることを恐れて、話すことに恥ずかしさを感じます。しかし、話すことが上達への一番の近道です。映画を観たり、歌を聴いたり、オンラインでおしゃべりしたりすることは、楽しい練習方法です。少しずつ、新しい言語は多くの扉を開いてくれるのです。

main: Volunteering means helping others without getting paid. People volunteer in many ways, such as cleaning parks, teaching children, or visiting elderly people. Volunteering is good for the community, but it is also good for the volunteers themselves. They meet new people, learn new skills, and feel proud of their work. Some students say volunteering helped them discover what they want to do in the future. You do not need special talents to volunteer. A kind heart and a little time are enough to make a difference.
Q1A: A. How to earn money.
Q1B: B. The joy and value of volunteering.
Q1C: C. Why parks are dirty.
Q1D: D. The life of elderly people.
A1: B. The joy and value of volunteering.
Q2: What do you need to volunteer?
Q2A: A. Special talents.
Q2B: B. A lot of money.
Q2C: C. A kind heart and a little time.
A2: C. A kind heart and a little time.
japanese: ボランティアとは、報酬を受け取らずに他の人を助けることです。人々は、公園の清掃、子どもたちに勉強を教えること、お年寄りを訪問することなど、さまざまな方法でボランティア活動をしています。ボランティアは地域社会にとって良いことですが、ボランティアをする人自身にとっても良いことです。新しい人と出会い、新しいスキルを学び、自分の活動に誇りを感じることができます。ボランティアのおかげで、将来何をしたいのかが見つかったと言う生徒もいます。ボランティアをするのに特別な才能は必要ありません。優しい心と少しの時間があれば、変化を生み出すのに十分なのです。

main: Having a pet can bring a lot of joy to a family. Dogs, cats, and other animals give us love and make our homes warmer. Playing with a pet can also reduce stress after a long day. However, taking care of a pet is a big responsibility. Pets need food, water, exercise, and visits to the doctor. Some people buy pets without thinking carefully and later give them up. Before getting a pet, we should make sure we can care for it for its whole life.
Q1A: A. Why cats are better than dogs.
Q1B: B. How to become an animal doctor.
Q1C: C. The history of zoos.
Q1D: D. The joy and responsibility of having a pet.
A1: D. The joy and responsibility of having a pet.
Q2: What should people do before getting a pet?
Q2A: A. Make sure they can care for it for its whole life.
Q2B: B. Buy many toys.
Q2C: C. Ask a doctor about their stress.
A2: A. Make sure they can care for it for its whole life.
japanese: ペットを飼うことは、家族に大きな喜びをもたらします。犬や猫、その他の動物は私たちに愛情を与え、家庭をより温かくしてくれます。また、ペットと遊ぶことで、長い1日の後のストレスを減らすこともできます。しかし、ペットの世話をすることは大きな責任です。ペットには食べ物、水、運動、そして動物病院での診察が必要です。よく考えずにペットを買い、後で手放してしまう人もいます。ペットを飼う前に、その一生を通して世話ができるかどうかを確かめるべきです。

main: Gardening is a relaxing hobby that anyone can start. You do not need a large yard; a few pots on a balcony are enough. Growing plants teaches patience because it takes time for seeds to become flowers or vegetables. It also helps us understand how nature works. Many gardeners say that touching soil and watching plants grow makes them feel calm. In addition, growing your own vegetables means you can enjoy fresh and safe food. Gardening is a small activity that brings big rewards.
Q1A: A. Gardening as a rewarding hobby.
Q1B: B. How to build a large yard.
Q1C: C. The dangers of soil.
A1: A. Gardening as a rewarding hobby.
Q2: What does growing plants teach us?
Q2A: A. How to sell vegetables.
Q2B: B. Patience.
Q2C: C. How to build a balcony.
A2: B. Patience.
japanese: ガーデニングは、誰でも始められるリラックスできる趣味です。広い庭は必要なく、ベランダにいくつかの鉢があれば十分です。種が花や野菜になるには時間がかかるので、植物を育てることは忍耐を教えてくれます。また、自然の仕組みを理解する助けにもなります。多くのガーデニング愛好家は、土に触れ、植物が育つのを見ていると心が落ち着くと言います。さらに、自分で野菜を育てれば、新鮮で安全な食べ物を楽しむことができます。ガーデニングは小さな活動ですが、大きな見返りをもたらしてくれるのです。

main: Traveling is one of the best ways to learn about the world. When we visit new places, we see different buildings, taste new foods, and hear new languages. These experiences help us understand that there are many ways of living. Travel can also teach us to solve problems, such as finding our way in an unknown city. Some people think travel must be expensive, but even a short trip to a nearby town can be exciting. What matters most is an open mind and a curious heart.
Q1A: A. How to save money on food.
Q1B: B. The history of airplanes.
Q1C: C. What we can learn from traveling.
A1: C. What we can learn from traveling.
Q2: According to the passage, what matters most in travel?
Q2A: A. Going to faraway countries.
Q2B: B. Spending a lot of money.
Q2C: C. Staying in expensive hotels.
Q2D: D. An open mind and a curious heart.
A2: D. An open mind and a curious heart.
japanese: 旅行は、世界について学ぶための最良の方法のひとつです。新しい場所を訪れると、異なる建物を目にし、新しい食べ物を味わい、新しい言語を耳にします。こうした経験は、さまざまな生き方があることを理解する助けになります。また、旅は、知らない街で道を探すといった問題を解決する力も教えてくれます。旅行はお金がかかるものだと考える人もいますが、近くの町への短い旅でもわくわくするものです。最も大切なのは、開かれた心と好奇心なのです。

main: Many people skip breakfast because they are busy in the morning. However, breakfast is often called the most important meal of the day. After a long night without food, our body and brain need energy to start working. Students who eat breakfast can concentrate better in class and remember more. A good breakfast does not have to be large or take a long time to make. A bowl of rice with miso soup, or bread with fruit and milk, is a great choice. Starting the day with breakfast helps us stay active until lunch.
Q1A: A. Why people are busy.
Q1B: B. The importance of eating breakfast.
Q1C: C. How to cook a large lunch.
Q1D: D. The history of miso soup.
A1: B. The importance of eating breakfast.
Q2: What does the passage say about a good breakfast?
Q2A: A. It must be very large.
Q2B: B. It takes a long time to make.
Q2C: C. It does not have to be large.
Q2D: D. It should only be bread.
A2: C. It does not have to be large.
japanese: 朝は忙しいため、朝食を抜く人がたくさんいます。しかし、朝食はしばしば1日で最も大切な食事と呼ばれます。食べ物のない長い夜の後、体と脳は活動を始めるためのエネルギーを必要としています。朝食を食べる生徒は、授業により集中でき、より多くのことを覚えることができます。良い朝食は、量が多い必要も、作るのに長い時間をかける必要もありません。ご飯とみそ汁、あるいはパンと果物と牛乳だけでも、すばらしい選択です。朝食で1日を始めると、昼食まで活動的でいることができるのです。

main: Water is essential for life. About sixty percent of the human body is made of water, and we lose some of it every day through sweat and breathing. If we do not drink enough, we may feel tired, get headaches, or have trouble thinking clearly. Many people drink sweet juice or soda when they are thirsty, but plain water is the healthiest choice. It is a good idea to carry a water bottle, especially on hot days or during sports. Drinking water regularly keeps our body working well.
Q1A: A. Why we need to drink water.
Q1B: B. How to make juice.
Q1C: C. The dangers of sports.
Q1D: D. Why hot days are fun.
A1: A. Why we need to drink water.
Q2: What is the healthiest drink according to the passage?
Q2A: A. Sweet juice.
Q2B: B. Soda.
Q2C: C. Sports drinks.
A2: D. Plain water.
japanese: 水は生命にとって欠かせないものです。人間の体の約60パーセントは水でできており、私たちは汗や呼吸を通して毎日その一部を失っています。十分に水を飲まないと、疲れを感じたり、頭が痛くなったり、はっきりと考えられなくなったりすることがあります。のどが渇いたときに甘いジュースや炭酸飲料を飲む人は多いですが、ただの水が最も健康的な選択です。特に暑い日やスポーツをするときは、水筒を持ち歩くのが良いでしょう。定期的に水を飲むことで、体がきちんと働き続けるのです。

main: Libraries are special places in every community. They offer thousands of books that anyone can borrow for free. But libraries are not only about books. Many of them also have computers, newspapers, movies, and quiet rooms for studying. Some libraries hold events such as storytelling for children or classes for adults. Librarians are always ready to help people find the information they need. In a world full of online information, libraries are still important because they give everyone equal access to knowledge.
Q1A: A. How to write a book.
Q1B: B. The history of newspapers.
Q1C: C. The value of libraries.
Q1D: D. Why online information is bad.
A1: C. The value of libraries.
Q2: Why are libraries still important today?
Q2A: A. They sell books at low prices.
Q2B: B. They give everyone equal access to knowledge.
Q2C: C. They are always noisy.
Q2D: D. They only have old books.
A2: B. They give everyone equal access to knowledge.
japanese: 図書館は、どの地域にとっても特別な場所です。図書館には、誰でも無料で借りられる何千冊もの本があります。しかし、図書館は本だけの場所ではありません。多くの図書館にはパソコン、新聞、映画、そして勉強のための静かな部屋もあります。子ども向けの読み聞かせや大人向けの講座などのイベントを開いている図書館もあります。司書は、人々が必要な情報を見つけるのをいつでも手伝ってくれます。インターネット上の情報があふれる世界においても、図書館は、すべての人に平等に知識を得る機会を与えてくれるため、今でも重要なのです。

main: Playing team sports teaches us many things that we cannot learn from books. In games like soccer, basketball, or volleyball, players must work together to win. Each member has a different role, and everyone needs to trust one another. Team sports also teach us how to deal with losing. After a hard defeat, players learn to support each other and try again. Communication is very important, too. These lessons are useful not only in sports but also at school, at work, and in daily life.
Q1A: A. How to win every game.
Q1B: B. Lessons we learn from team sports.
Q1C: C. The rules of soccer.
A1: B. Lessons we learn from team sports.
Q2: What do players learn after a hard defeat?
Q2A: A. To quit the team.
Q2B: B. To blame other players.
Q2C: C. To support each other and try again.
A2: C. To support each other and try again.
japanese: チームスポーツをすることで、本からは学べない多くのことを学ぶことができます。サッカー、バスケットボール、バレーボールのような競技では、勝つために選手たちが協力しなければなりません。メンバーそれぞれに異なる役割があり、全員が互いを信頼する必要があります。チームスポーツは、負けたときにどう向き合うかも教えてくれます。つらい敗北の後、選手たちは互いに支え合い、再び挑戦することを学びます。コミュニケーションもとても大切です。これらの教訓は、スポーツだけでなく、学校や職場、そして日常生活においても役に立つのです。

main: Drawing is a wonderful way to express ourselves. Some people think only talented artists can draw, but that is not true. Anyone can pick up a pencil and start. Drawing helps us look at the world more carefully, because we notice shapes, colors, and small details. It can also be a way to share feelings that are hard to put into words. Many people find that drawing for just a few minutes calms their mind. The goal is not to make a perfect picture but to enjoy the process.
Q1A: A. How to sell paintings.
Q1B: B. The history of pencils.
Q1C: C. Why only artists should draw.
A1: D. The joy of drawing.
Q2: What is the goal of drawing according to the passage?
Q2A: A. To enjoy the process.
Q2B: B. To make a perfect picture.
Q2C: C. To become famous.
A2: A. To enjoy the process.
japanese: 絵を描くことは、自分を表現するすばらしい方法です。才能のある芸術家だけが絵を描けると考える人もいますが、それは正しくありません。誰でも鉛筆を手に取って始めることができます。絵を描くと、形や色、細かい部分に気づくようになるため、世界をより注意深く見る助けになります。また、言葉にするのが難しい気持ちを伝える手段にもなります。ほんの数分絵を描くだけで心が落ち着くと感じる人はたくさんいます。目標は完璧な絵を描くことではなく、その過程を楽しむことなのです。

main: Eating meals together as a family is a simple but valuable habit. At the dinner table, family members can talk about their day, share their worries, and laugh together. Studies show that children who often eat with their families tend to do better at school and feel more secure. These days, many families are busy, and each person often eats at a different time. Even so, having a meal together once or twice a week can make a big difference. Good food tastes even better when shared.
Q1A: A. The value of family meals.
Q1B: B. How to cook dinner quickly.
Q1C: C. Why children are busy.
Q1D: D. The best restaurants in town.
A1: A. The value of family meals.
Q2: What do studies show about children who often eat with their families?
Q2A: A. They eat too much.
Q2B: B. They tend to do better at school.
Q2C: C. They do not like talking.
A2: B. They tend to do better at school.
japanese: 家族そろって食事をすることは、シンプルですが価値のある習慣です。食卓では、家族がその日の出来事を話したり、悩みを打ち明けたり、一緒に笑ったりすることができます。研究によると、家族とよく一緒に食事をする子どもは、学校での成績が良く、より安心感を持つ傾向があります。最近では多くの家庭が忙しく、それぞれが別々の時間に食事をすることがよくあります。それでも、週に1、2回一緒に食事をするだけで、大きな違いが生まれます。おいしい料理は、分かち合うことでさらにおいしくなるのです。

main: Keeping a diary is an easy habit that can improve our lives. By writing down what happened each day, we can remember special moments that we might otherwise forget. A diary is also a safe place to express our feelings. When we are angry or sad, writing can help us calm down and understand ourselves better. Some people write about their goals and check their progress. There are no rules for writing a diary. Even a few lines before bed can become a precious record of our lives.
Q1A: A. How to become a writer.
Q1B: B. The benefits of keeping a diary.
Q1C: C. Why feelings are dangerous.
Q1D: D. The rules of good writing.
A1: B. The benefits of keeping a diary.
Q2: What does the passage say about writing a diary?
Q2A: A. It must be long.
Q2B: B. It should follow strict rules.
Q2C: C. There are no rules for it.
Q2D: D. It should be written in the morning.
A2: C. There are no rules for it.
japanese: 日記をつけることは、私たちの生活を豊かにできる手軽な習慣です。毎日の出来事を書き留めることで、書かなければ忘れてしまうかもしれない特別な瞬間を覚えておくことができます。日記はまた、自分の気持ちを表現できる安心な場所でもあります。怒っているときや悲しいとき、書くことは心を落ち着かせ、自分自身をより深く理解する助けになります。自分の目標について書き、その進み具合を確認する人もいます。日記の書き方に決まりはありません。寝る前の数行だけでも、人生の貴重な記録になるのです。

main: Learning how to save money is an important skill for young people. When we get money, it is easy to spend it all on snacks, games, or clothes. However, if we save a little each time, we can buy something bigger later or prepare for an emergency. One good way to start is to set a clear goal, such as a new bike. Writing down what we spend also helps us notice where our money goes. Saving money teaches patience and helps us plan for the future.
Q1A: A. How to spend money on games.
Q1B: B. Why clothes are expensive.
Q1C: C. The importance of saving money.
A1: C. The importance of saving money.
Q2: What is one good way to start saving money?
Q2A: A. Spend it all at once.
Q2B: B. Set a clear goal.
Q2C: C. Buy more snacks.
A2: B. Set a clear goal.
japanese: お金を貯める方法を学ぶことは、若い人たちにとって大切なスキルです。お金を手に入れると、お菓子やゲーム、服にすべて使ってしまいがちです。しかし、毎回少しずつ貯めれば、後でもっと大きなものを買ったり、緊急時に備えたりすることができます。始めるのに良い方法のひとつは、新しい自転車のようにはっきりとした目標を立てることです。使ったお金を書き留めることも、お金の行き先に気づく助けになります。お金を貯めることは忍耐を教えてくれ、将来の計画を立てる助けにもなるのです。

main: Small acts of kindness can make a big difference. Holding the door for someone, saying thank you, or helping a classmate with homework may seem simple. However, these actions can brighten someone's day. Kindness also spreads. When people are treated kindly, they are more likely to be kind to others. Scientists have found that helping others makes the helper feel happier, too. We do not need money or special skills to be kind. All we need is to notice the people around us and care about them.
Q1A: A. How to do homework.
Q1B: B. Why doors are important.
Q1C: C. The history of good manners.
Q1D: D. The power of small acts of kindness.
A1: D. The power of small acts of kindness.
Q2: What have scientists found about helping others?
Q2A: A. It makes the helper feel happier.
Q2B: B. It costs a lot of money.
Q2C: C. It needs special skills.
A2: A. It makes the helper feel happier.
japanese: 小さな親切が大きな違いを生むことがあります。誰かのためにドアを押さえておくこと、「ありがとう」と言うこと、クラスメートの宿題を手伝うことは、簡単なことに思えるかもしれません。しかし、こうした行動は誰かの1日を明るくすることができます。親切はまた、広がっていくものです。親切にされた人は、他の人にも親切にしやすくなります。科学者たちは、他人を助けることで、助けた人自身もより幸せを感じることを発見しました。親切にするのに、お金や特別なスキルは必要ありません。必要なのは、周りの人々に気づき、気にかけることだけなのです。

main: Museums are like time machines. When we walk through a museum, we can see tools used thousands of years ago, famous paintings, and even dinosaur bones. Seeing real objects helps us understand history and science better than just reading about them in textbooks. Many museums now have interactive displays where visitors can touch, listen, and try things for themselves. Some also offer free days for students. Visiting a museum is a fun way to learn, and each visit can spark new interests and questions.
Q1A: A. How to build a time machine.
Q1B: B. The value of visiting museums.
Q1C: C. Why textbooks are boring.
A1: B. The value of visiting museums.
Q2: What do many museums now have?
Q2A: A. Only old paintings.
Q2B: B. No rooms for students.
Q2C: C. Interactive displays.
A2: C. Interactive displays.
japanese: 博物館はタイムマシンのようなものです。博物館の中を歩くと、何千年も前に使われていた道具や有名な絵画、さらには恐竜の骨まで見ることができます。本物を見ることは、教科書で読むだけよりも歴史や科学をよく理解する助けになります。現在では多くの博物館に、来館者が自分で触ったり、聞いたり、試したりできる体験型の展示があります。学生向けに無料の日を設けている博物館もあります。博物館を訪れることは楽しい学びの方法であり、訪れるたびに新しい興味や疑問が生まれるかもしれません。

main: The ocean covers more than seventy percent of the Earth's surface, but we know surprisingly little about it. Most of the deep sea has never been explored by humans. It is dark and cold there, and the water pressure is extremely strong. Even so, scientists have found strange creatures living there, such as fish that make their own light. Special robots and submarines are now helping researchers study these areas. Some scientists believe there are still thousands of unknown species in the deep sea waiting to be discovered.
Q1A: A. The mysteries of the deep sea.
Q1B: B. How to catch fish.
Q1C: C. Why the ocean is warm.
A1: A. The mysteries of the deep sea.
Q2: What have scientists found in the deep sea?
Q2A: A. Warm and bright water.
Q2B: B. Many human cities.
Q2C: C. Fish that make their own light.
A2: C. Fish that make their own light.
japanese: 海は地球の表面の70パーセント以上を覆っていますが、私たちは海について驚くほど少ししか知りません。深海のほとんどは、人間によって探検されたことがありません。そこは暗くて冷たく、水圧は非常に強力です。それでも、科学者たちは、自分で光を出す魚など、そこに暮らす不思議な生き物を発見してきました。現在では、特別なロボットや潜水艇が、研究者たちがこうした場所を調べるのに役立っています。深海には、発見されるのを待っている未知の生物がまだ何千種もいると考える科学者もいます。

main: Bicycles are a convenient and eco-friendly way to get around. Riding a bike does not produce any gas that pollutes the air, and it costs much less than using a car. It is also great exercise that makes our legs and heart stronger. In some countries, such as the Netherlands, there are more bicycles than people. Cities there have special roads only for bikes. When riding, however, we must follow traffic rules and wear a helmet. Safe cycling helps both people and the planet.
Q1A: A. The benefits of riding bicycles.
Q1B: B. How to drive a car.
Q1C: C. The history of the Netherlands.
A1: A. The benefits of riding bicycles.
Q2: What must we do when riding a bike?
Q2A: A. Ride as fast as possible.
Q2B: B. Ride on the sidewalk.
Q2C: C. Carry heavy bags.
Q2D: D. Follow traffic rules and wear a helmet.
A2: D. Follow traffic rules and wear a helmet.
japanese: 自転車は、便利で環境にやさしい移動手段です。自転車に乗っても、空気を汚すガスはまったく出ませんし、車を使うよりもずっとお金がかかりません。また、足や心臓を強くしてくれる、すばらしい運動にもなります。オランダのように、人口よりも自転車の数が多い国もあります。そこの都市には、自転車専用の道路があります。しかし、自転車に乗るときは、交通ルールを守り、ヘルメットをかぶらなければなりません。安全に自転車に乗ることは、人と地球の両方のためになるのです。

main: Bees are small, but they play a big role in our lives. As they fly from flower to flower to collect nectar, they carry pollen. This helps plants produce fruits and seeds. In fact, about one-third of the food we eat depends on bees and other insects like them. Without bees, foods such as apples, strawberries, and almonds would become rare and expensive. Sadly, the number of bees is decreasing because of chemicals and the loss of flowers. Planting flowers in gardens is one way to help them.
Q1A: A. How to make honey.
Q1B: B. Why insects are dangerous.
Q1C: C. The important role of bees.
A1: C. The important role of bees.
Q2: Why is the number of bees decreasing?
Q2A: A. Because of chemicals and the loss of flowers.
Q2B: B. Because people eat too many apples.
Q2C: C. Because there are too many gardens.
Q2D: D. Because bees do not like fruit.
A2: A. Because of chemicals and the loss of flowers.
japanese: ミツバチは小さな生き物ですが、私たちの生活の中で大きな役割を果たしています。花の蜜を集めるために花から花へと飛び回るとき、ミツバチは花粉を運びます。これによって、植物は果物や種を作ることができます。実は、私たちが食べる食べ物の約3分の1は、ミツバチやそれに似た昆虫に頼っているのです。ミツバチがいなければ、リンゴ、イチゴ、アーモンドのような食べ物は珍しく、高価なものになってしまうでしょう。残念なことに、化学物質や花の減少のために、ミツバチの数は減ってきています。庭に花を植えることは、ミツバチを助けるひとつの方法です。

main: Asking questions is one of the best ways to learn. Young children ask 'Why?' hundreds of times a day, and that is how they understand the world. As we grow older, however, many of us stop asking questions because we are afraid of looking foolish. This is a pity. Great discoveries often begin with a simple question, such as 'Why does an apple fall?' Teachers are usually happy when students ask questions. The next time you do not understand something, raise your hand and ask.
Q1A: A. Why children are foolish.
Q1B: B. The history of apples.
Q1C: C. How teachers grade tests.
Q1D: D. The importance of asking questions.
A1: D. The importance of asking questions.
Q2: Why do many people stop asking questions as they grow older?
Q2A: A. They know everything.
Q2B: B. They are afraid of looking foolish.
Q2C: C. Teachers do not allow it.
A2: B. They are afraid of looking foolish.
japanese: 質問をすることは、学ぶための最良の方法のひとつです。幼い子どもは1日に何百回も「なぜ？」と尋ね、そうやって世界を理解していきます。しかし、成長するにつれて、多くの人はばかだと思われるのを恐れて、質問をしなくなってしまいます。これは残念なことです。偉大な発見は、「なぜリンゴは落ちるのだろう？」のような単純な疑問から始まることがよくあります。先生たちはたいてい、生徒が質問をすると喜びます。今度何かわからないことがあったら、手を挙げて質問してみましょう。

main: Festivals are an important part of culture around the world. In Japan, summer festivals are famous for fireworks, dancing, and food stands. In other countries, people celebrate with colorful parades, music, and special meals. Many festivals have a long history and are connected to seasons, harvests, or religion. They bring people of all ages together and help communities stay close. Joining a local festival is also a good way to learn about the traditions of a place. Festivals keep old customs alive for future generations.
Q1A: A. The role of festivals in culture.
Q1B: B. How to make fireworks.
Q1C: C. Why food stands are expensive.
A1: A. The role of festivals in culture.
Q2: What is one good way to learn about the traditions of a place?
Q2A: A. Reading about fireworks.
Q2B: B. Staying at home.
Q2C: C. Joining a local festival.
A2: C. Joining a local festival.
japanese: 祭りは、世界中の文化の重要な一部です。日本では、夏祭りは花火や踊り、屋台で有名です。ほかの国々では、人々は色とりどりのパレードや音楽、特別な料理でお祝いをします。多くの祭りには長い歴史があり、季節や収穫、宗教と結びついています。祭りはあらゆる年代の人々を集め、地域の人々の結びつきを保つ助けになります。地元の祭りに参加することは、その土地の伝統について学ぶ良い方法でもあります。祭りは、古い習慣を未来の世代のために守り続けているのです。

main: In the age of email and text messages, handwritten letters have become rare. However, many people still feel special when they receive one. A handwritten letter shows that the writer spent time and effort thinking about the reader. The shape of the letters and the choice of paper also show the writer's personality. Unlike messages on a screen, letters can be kept in a box and read again many years later. Sending a thank-you card or a birthday letter by hand is a warm way to show you care.
Q1A: A. How to send an email.
Q1B: B. The special value of handwritten letters.
Q1C: C. The history of paper.
Q1D: D. Why text messages are fast.
A1: B. The special value of handwritten letters.
Q2: What does a handwritten letter show?
Q2A: A. The writer did not have a phone.
Q2B: B. The writer was in a hurry.
Q2C: C. The writer spent time and effort.
A2: C. The writer spent time and effort.
japanese: メールやメッセージアプリの時代において、手書きの手紙は珍しいものになりました。しかし、今でも多くの人が、手紙を受け取ると特別な気持ちになります。手書きの手紙は、書き手が読み手のことを考えて時間と労力をかけたことを示しています。文字の形や便せんの選び方にも、書き手の人柄が表れます。画面上のメッセージと違い、手紙は箱にしまっておき、何年も後に読み返すことができます。お礼のカードや誕生日の手紙を手書きで送ることは、相手を思う気持ちを伝える温かい方法なのです。

main: Board games have been enjoyed for thousands of years. Games like chess and shogi require careful thinking and planning. Players must imagine what their opponent will do next. This helps train the brain and improve problem-solving skills. Board games are also a great way to spend time with family and friends. Unlike video games, which people often play alone, board games bring people face to face around a table. Winning is fun, but learning to lose politely is an important lesson, too.
Q1A: A. Why video games are bad.
Q1B: B. The history of chess.
Q1C: C. The benefits of board games.
Q1D: D. How to win every game.
A1: C. The benefits of board games.
Q2: What must players imagine in games like chess and shogi?
Q2A: A. What their opponent will do next.
Q2B: B. How to cook dinner.
Q2C: C. Where to buy the game.
Q2D: D. How long the game will last.
A2: A. What their opponent will do next.
japanese: ボードゲームは何千年もの間、楽しまれてきました。チェスや将棋のようなゲームには、注意深く考え、計画を立てることが求められます。プレーヤーは、相手が次に何をするかを想像しなければなりません。これは脳を鍛え、問題解決能力を高める助けになります。ボードゲームは、家族や友だちと時間を過ごすすばらしい方法でもあります。一人で遊ぶことが多いテレビゲームと違い、ボードゲームは人々をテーブルの周りで向かい合わせてくれます。勝つことは楽しいですが、礼儀正しく負けることを学ぶのも大切な教訓です。

main: Taking photos is easier than ever because almost everyone has a camera on their phone. Photos help us save memories of trips, friends, and special days. But photography can be more than just pressing a button. Good photographers pay attention to light, angles, and the story behind each picture. Trying to take better photos teaches us to look closely at ordinary things, like a shadow on a wall or a cat sleeping in the sun. Sometimes, the most beautiful pictures are found in everyday life.
Q1A: A. How to buy a camera.
Q1B: B. The art of photography.
Q1C: C. Why cats sleep in the sun.
A1: B. The art of photography.
Q2: According to the passage, where are the most beautiful pictures sometimes found?
Q2A: A. In expensive studios.
Q2B: B. In faraway countries.
Q2C: C. In famous museums.
A2: D. In everyday life.
japanese: ほとんど誰もがスマートフォンにカメラを持っているので、写真を撮ることはかつてないほど簡単になりました。写真は、旅行や友だち、特別な日の思い出を残す助けになります。しかし、写真はただシャッターを押すだけのものではありません。優れた写真家は、光や角度、そしてそれぞれの写真の背後にある物語に注意を払います。より良い写真を撮ろうとすると、壁に映る影や日なたで眠る猫のような、ありふれたものをよく見るようになります。最も美しい写真は、日常生活の中に見つかることもあるのです。

main: Keeping your room clean has more benefits than you might think. A tidy room makes it easier to find things, so you do not waste time looking for your keys or homework. It can also help you focus when you study, because there are fewer things to distract you. Some people say that cleaning their room makes them feel refreshed and more positive. The trick is to clean a little every day instead of waiting until the mess becomes too big. Putting things back after using them is a good first step.
Q1A: A. The benefits of keeping your room clean.
Q1B: B. How to buy furniture.
Q1C: C. Why homework is difficult.
A1: A. The benefits of keeping your room clean.
Q2: What is the trick to keeping a room clean?
Q2A: A. Clean only once a year.
Q2B: B. Move to a bigger room.
Q2C: C. Clean a little every day.
Q2D: D. Ask others to clean it.
A2: C. Clean a little every day.
japanese: 部屋をきれいに保つことには、あなたが思っている以上にたくさんの利点があります。整理された部屋では物が見つけやすいので、鍵や宿題を探して時間を無駄にすることがありません。また、気を散らすものが少なくなるので、勉強するときに集中しやすくなります。部屋を掃除するとすっきりして、前向きな気持ちになれると言う人もいます。こつは、散らかりがひどくなるまで待つのではなく、毎日少しずつ掃除することです。使った物を元の場所に戻すことが、良い第一歩になります。

main: Older people have lived through many experiences, and their stories are a treasure. Grandparents can tell us what life was like when they were young, such as how they went to school or what games they played. These stories help us understand how much the world has changed. They also teach us lessons about hard times and how to overcome them. Unfortunately, many young people rarely talk with elderly people. Spending time listening to them can build a bridge between generations and give us wisdom that books cannot.
Q1A: A. How schools have changed.
Q1B: B. Why young people are busy.
Q1C: C. The value of listening to older people.
A1: C. The value of listening to older people.
Q2: What can older people's stories teach us?
Q2A: A. How to play video games.
Q2B: B. Lessons about hard times and how to overcome them.
Q2C: C. How to write books.
A2: B. Lessons about hard times and how to overcome them.
japanese: お年寄りはたくさんの経験をしてきており、その話は宝物です。祖父母は、どのように学校に通っていたか、どんな遊びをしていたかなど、若いころの生活がどのようなものだったかを話してくれます。こうした話は、世界がどれほど変わったかを理解する助けになります。また、苦しい時期のことや、それをどう乗り越えたかについての教訓も教えてくれます。残念ながら、多くの若者はお年寄りと話すことがめったにありません。彼らの話に耳を傾ける時間を持つことは、世代と世代の間に橋をかけ、本では得られない知恵を与えてくれるのです。

main: Many people feel sad when it rains, but rainy days are important. Rain gives water to rivers, forests, and farms. Without it, plants could not grow and we would not have enough food or drinking water. Rainy days can also be enjoyable. The sound of rain is relaxing, and it is a perfect time to read a book, watch a movie, or try a new recipe at home. In Japan, the rainy season brings beautiful flowers like hydrangeas. Instead of complaining about the rain, we can find ways to enjoy it.
Q1A: A. Why rain is dangerous.
Q1B: B. How to make a movie.
Q1C: C. The history of Japan.
Q1D: D. The value and fun of rainy days.
A1: D. The value and fun of rainy days.
Q2: Which flower does the passage mention?
Q2A: A. Hydrangeas.
Q2B: B. Roses.
Q2C: C. Sunflowers.
A2: A. Hydrangeas.
japanese: 雨が降ると悲しい気持ちになる人は多いですが、雨の日は大切です。雨は川や森、農地に水を与えます。雨がなければ植物は育たず、私たちは十分な食べ物や飲み水を得ることができないでしょう。雨の日は楽しむこともできます。雨の音は心を落ち着かせてくれますし、家で本を読んだり、映画を観たり、新しいレシピに挑戦したりするのにぴったりの時間です。日本では、梅雨の季節にアジサイのような美しい花が咲きます。雨に文句を言うのではなく、雨を楽しむ方法を見つけることができるのです。

main: Many students study for hours without a break, believing it is the best way to learn. However, research shows that our brain cannot stay focused for a long time. After about forty-five minutes, concentration usually starts to drop. Taking a short break of five to ten minutes can refresh the mind. During a break, it is good to stand up, stretch, or look out the window. Checking a smartphone, however, may make it harder to return to studying. Short, regular breaks help us learn more effectively.
Q1A: A. Why students hate studying.
Q1B: B. How to use a smartphone.
Q1C: C. The importance of taking breaks while studying.
A1: C. The importance of taking breaks while studying.
Q2: What is a good thing to do during a break?
Q2A: A. Check a smartphone for a long time.
Q2B: B. Stand up and stretch.
Q2C: C. Start a new subject.
Q2D: D. Go to sleep for three hours.
A2: B. Stand up and stretch.
japanese: 多くの生徒は、それが最も良い学習方法だと信じて、休憩をとらずに何時間も勉強します。しかし、研究によると、私たちの脳は長い時間集中し続けることができません。およそ45分たつと、たいてい集中力は落ち始めます。5～10分の短い休憩をとると、頭をリフレッシュさせることができます。休憩中は、立ち上がったり、ストレッチをしたり、窓の外を眺めたりするのが良いでしょう。しかし、スマートフォンを見ると、勉強に戻りにくくなるかもしれません。短い休憩を定期的にとることで、より効率的に学ぶことができるのです。
